subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a model-callable, current-session-only self-compaction action as a supported core agent capability?
rationale: Existing manual, automatic, and operator compaction do not settle whether an in-run model may intentionally mutate and restart its own session; that choice defines the permanent authorization and recovery contract.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow current-session action
options.body: Adopt the current-session-only design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95272 after resolving its merge state and reviewing its abort/recovery semantics.

options.title: Keep compaction external-only
options.body: Retain automatic, user-command, and administrator paths while declining a model-callable self-mutation surface in core.

options.title: Define a broader lifecycle API first
options.body: Pause the narrow action until maintainers specify a cohesive agent lifecycle and continuation API that includes voluntary compaction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow current-session action
recommendation.body: Adopt the current-session-only design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95272 after resolving its merge state and reviewing its abort/recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the relevant tool surface and previously documented the current boundary between session status, gateway compaction, and embedded recovery.
